title: Hexagon Dedicated pilot check-in — autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
summary: Weekly pilot check-in with Hexagon on Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive scaling. Reviewed new Grafana dashboard panels (desired vs bounded replicas, bound-hit rate, queue depth/p95 latency) and walked through two incidents where the deployment hit max bound during the morning ramp, leading to queue buildup. Customer feedback: bounds are doing what they want (cost ceiling), but they need clearer UX/alerts when they’re saturating at max and a recommended way to pick min/max. Bug report: predictive signal appeared to return “null/0” briefly, and the Console/audit log timeline showed confusing “desired=0” even though bounded replicas stayed at min; Redwood to validate and confirm hotfix timeline. Agreed on config tweaks: increase max from 24→28 for pilot week, raise min from 10→12 during weekday business hours (manual for now), keep predictive mode enabled but with more conservative scale-down/cooldown. Next steps include sharing an updated alert rule proposal for sustained max-bound saturation and giving Hexagon a short guide on interpreting bounded vs desired metrics.
topics: Pilot results recap (last 7 days): latency during daily ramp, queue depth spikes
Dashboard review: desired vs bounded, bound-hit counters, scale event timeline
Predictive mode behavior and safety guardrails (cooldowns, reactive override)
Config tweaks: min/max adjustments, cooldown/step sizing
Bug report: predictor null/0 and confusing audit log entries
Alerts & comms: when to page vs when to notify CS
questions: Can we get an explicit signal/flag in Console when we’re capped by max so product teams stop blaming the model?
If prediction is wrong, does reactive scaling override it immediately or after cooldown?
When region capacity is tight, how do you surface that min can’t be met (and what’s the SLA language)?
Can we schedule different bounds for business hours vs off-hours (even if it’s manual/IaC at first)?
action_items: Vanessa Ortiz — pull scale event logs for hexagon-prod-us-east and confirm whether forecast provider returned null around 2025-07-08 ~14:05Z; report back in Slack/email — due 2025-07-10
Sergio Costa — share direct Grafana link and annotate the bound-hit + queue depth panels with a short ‘how to read this’ note — due 2025-07-10
Rachel Kim — send recommended pilot config proposal (min/max + cooldown) and a short write-up on choosing bounds for SLA vs cost cap — due 2025-07-11
Liam O'Rourke — open support/eng ticket for ‘Console shows desired=0 when predictor null’ with screenshots from Hexagon, include timestamps — due 2025-07-09
Priya Desai (Hexagon) — apply max 24→28 change for the pilot week and confirm change window; share results after Thursday ramp — due 2025-07-10
next_steps: Hexagon to temporarily raise max bound to 28 GPUs for the week to reduce queueing during the morning ramp while keeping cost ceiling predictable.
Redwood to validate predictor null/0 behavior and confirm whether this is a data issue, display issue, or autoscaler decision path; provide an ETA for fix if needed.
Redwood to propose alert thresholds for sustained max-bound saturation (e.g., bound-hit rate + queue depth) and align on paging vs email notifications.
Schedule next check-in (30 min) to review Thursday ramp and any changes in bound-hit rate and p95 latency.
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: Hexagon Dedicated pilot check-in — autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
Date: 2025-07-09
Start time: 16:03 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes

Attendees
- Redwood Inference: Rachel Kim (CS), Liam O’Rourke (TAM), Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet), Sergio Costa (Obs)
- Hexagon Support Systems: Priya Desai (Platform Eng), Mark Feldman (SRE), Jenna Wu (Eng Mgr), Omar Rahman (FinOps)

---

[00:00] Rachel Kim: Alright, cool. I think we’re recording. Um, thanks everyone for making time. Goal today is basically look at the dashboards from the pilot, talk through the max-bound hits you saw, and then if we want to tweak min/max or predictive settings before Thursday’s ramp.

[00:18] Priya Desai: Yep. Sounds good.

[00:20] Mark Feldman: Yeah, and also, we have like one weird thing we saw in the UI where it said desired went to zero. We want to make sure that’s not actually happening.

[00:30] Rachel Kim: Yep, definitely. We’ll get into that.

[00:33] Liam O'Rourke: I’ll take notes and we can turn those into a ticket.

[00:36] Sergio Costa: I can share screen if that helps, but Priya I think you already have the Grafana link.

[00:41] Priya Desai: I do. I can also share, either way.

[00:44] Rachel Kim: Sergio, go ahead and share. It’s easier if we’re all aligned.

[00:49] Sergio Costa: Cool. Sharing… you should see “Dedicated Autoscaling — Bounds Pilot” dashboard.

[01:02] Sergio Costa: Top left is desired replicas versus bounded replicas. So “desired_unbounded” is what the autoscaler loop computes pre-clamp. “desired_bounded” is post clamp to min/max. Then we have the “bound_hit_total” counters, broken down by min-bound and max-bound.

[01:21] Omar Rahman: Just to confirm, bounded equals what we actually pay for, right?

[01:25] Vanessa Ortiz: Bounded equals what we request/target for the fleet for your pool, yeah. In practice that maps pretty closely to billable capacity for Dedicated. There are a few nuances with warm spares, but for the pilot, yes, that’s the number to watch.

[01:39] Omar Rahman: Okay, good.

[01:41] Rachel Kim: And that’s the contractual behavior you asked for — never exceed max, never drop below min.

[01:47] Jenna Wu: So what happened yesterday morning is we had the assistant feature ramp at like 9am local, and we saw p95 spike. We think it queued.

[01:58] Mark Feldman: Yeah. Queue depth went, like, from basically zero to 300-ish requests waiting, and it stayed there for, I don’t know, 12 minutes.

[02:08] Sergio Costa: Yep, that’s the middle panel here. Queue depth is the blue line, and p95 latency is the orange. Let me zoom into July 8.

[02:17] Sergio Costa: Okay, here. You see at 13:55 UTC it starts rising.

[02:23] Priya Desai: That’s 8:55 central, yep.

[02:27] Vanessa Ortiz: And if you look at desired vs bounded right above it, desired_unbounded jumped to 31 for a bit, but bounded is flat at 24, which is your current max.

[02:38] Mark Feldman: Right. That’s the point. We got capped. Which is fine, that’s the whole point of the max, but we need to know it’s the cap doing it, not like the model got slower.

[02:50] Rachel Kim: Makes sense. So you want more explicit “you are at max bound” surfaced, like in Console and an alert?

[02:57] Mark Feldman: Yeah. Like, we want to route that as “capacity constrained by policy.” Otherwise our on-call just sees latency and they’re like, “is Redwood melting?”

[03:07] Liam O'Rourke: Totally. We have a bound-hit rate metric and we can wire an alert on that plus queue depth.

[03:13] Omar Rahman: Plus for me, from finance side, I’d rather get an email saying, “you hit max, you’re saturating,” than someone quietly bumping max.

[03:21] Rachel Kim: Yup. That’s consistent with what other pilot customers are asking for.

[03:26] Sergio Costa: One thing to call out — bound_hit_total is a counter so it always goes up, but we can also chart a rate, like bound hits per minute, and show the percentage of time you’re clamped.

[03:39] Priya Desai: The way we interpret it right now is kind of manual, yeah.

[03:44] Vanessa Ortiz: The other nuance: reactive scaling is still trying to scale you up. It’s just clamped. So that’s why queue builds. Predictive can help you avoid the queue buildup by scaling earlier, but it can’t exceed max. So if max is just too low for the ramp, you either raise max or accept the queue.

[04:03] Jenna Wu: For the pilot, we can raise max temporarily. We just need it to be intentional and auditable.

[04:09] Rachel Kim: Great. Before we decide the number, can we talk about the second incident? Mark, you mentioned there were two.

[04:15] Mark Feldman: Yeah, the other one was Friday. Similar thing. But what was weirder on Friday was we saw the “desired” line drop to zero in the Console view. But actual pods didn’t go to zero. It freaked us out.

[04:28] Vanessa Ortiz: Okay, that’s the bug report. Let’s dig in.

[04:31] Sergio Costa: In Grafana, I don’t see bounded ever below 10, which is your min. You can see bounded stays 10 overnight and then steps up.

[04:41] Mark Feldman: Right, bounded stayed 10. But in the audit log timeline, it said something like “desired=0 reason prediction null,” or that’s what it looked like.

[04:51] Liam O'Rourke: Do you have a screenshot? If not, we can pull the audit entries.

[04:55] Priya Desai: I can grab a screenshot after. It was in the console’s scaling events tab. It might have been like a brief blip.

[05:03] Vanessa Ortiz: I want to be super clear: autoscaler should never actually request below min. Clamp happens after whatever signal, reactive or predictive. But it’s possible the unbounded desired computed was zero if the predictor returned null or “0” and we’re accidentally plotting the pre-clamp value in Console.

[05:20] Mark Feldman: Yeah, that’s what it felt like. Like the UI was showing the raw thing, not the bounded.

[05:25] Sergio Costa: That’s consistent. Grafana is pulling both series and labeling them, but the Console might only show one.

[05:32] Rachel Kim: Okay, so action item: Vanessa, can you check logs around that timestamp and confirm what the forecast provider returned and what the bounded decision was?

[05:41] Vanessa Ortiz: Yes. If you can give me approximate time, I’ll pull the “scaling_decision” events. We log requested desired and bounded desired and the reason.

[05:51] Mark Feldman: I think it was Friday around 2pm our time. So, 19:00 UTC maybe.

[05:58] Vanessa Ortiz: Got it.

[06:00] Rachel Kim: Liam, can you open a ticket once we have the screenshot? We want a paper trail.

[06:05] Liam O'Rourke: Yep.

[06:07] Jenna Wu: Also can we talk about predictive? Because right now it’s like… we like that it scales ahead, but we’re still seeing a little oscillation.

[06:16] Vanessa Ortiz: Sure. When you say oscillation, do you mean it scales up then immediately scales down?

[06:21] Jenna Wu: Yeah. Like it ramps to 20, then drops to 14, then back to 18, within like 10 minutes.

[06:29] Mark Feldman: It’s not terrible but it creates noise in our internal metrics.

[06:34] Vanessa Ortiz: That’s usually cooldown and dampening settings. In the pilot, we set a conservative scale-up but scale-down might be too aggressive. We can set a minimum scale-down interval, like 15 minutes, and/or require sustained low utilization before scaling down.

[06:50] Priya Desai: Is that on your side or ours?

[06:52] Vanessa Ortiz: Today it’s config in the scaling policy, but not all knobs are exposed in Console yet. We can apply it for the pilot via admin config and then later you’ll have it.

[07:02] Omar Rahman: From cost perspective, we don’t mind staying high a little longer as long as we don’t exceed max. Like, I’d rather pay for an extra 15 minutes than have the user experience bounce.

[07:13] Rachel Kim: That’s good feedback. So we can bias toward slower scale-down.

[07:17] Sergio Costa: Also, the scale event timeline panel shows those up/down events. If we add a “scale_down_suppressed” reason, it’ll be easier to see when cooldown prevented a change.

[07:29] Mark Feldman: Yeah, more reasons is better.

[07:32] Rachel Kim: Okay. Let’s talk about the max bound. Right now it’s set to 24 GPUs, correct?

[07:38] Priya Desai: Correct. We started at min 10, max 24.

[07:41] Vanessa Ortiz: And the desired_unbounded during the ramp wants around 30 to 32 based on queue depth and utilization signals.

[07:49] Priya Desai: If we set max to 28, does that materially reduce queue?

[07:55] Vanessa Ortiz: It should. The relationship isn’t perfectly linear because it depends on batch sizes and model behavior, but based on your throughput, each GPU adds about X tokens/sec. I’d expect queue depth to peak lower and clear faster. It may not eliminate it if demand truly needs 32.

[08:11] Jenna Wu: For this week, can we do 28 and see? Then we decide if we need 30.

[08:17] Omar Rahman: 28 is okay for pilot, but we need to put a change control around it. Like, we only bump it with FinOps approval.

[08:25] Rachel Kim: Totally. We’ll treat it as a config change with audit entry.

[08:30] Liam O'Rourke: Also, we can set an alert that triggers when you’re clamped at max for, say, 5 minutes plus queue depth above threshold. That way it’s a decision, not a surprise.

[08:43] Mark Feldman: I like that.

[08:45] Sergio Costa: Do you have a preferred paging route? Like do we page Mark’s on-call, or is it an email to a distro?

[08:51] Mark Feldman: For now, email. If it pages, it’ll be too noisy. Maybe later if it’s truly customer-impacting.

[09:00] Rachel Kim: Okay, email alert for now.

[09:03] Priya Desai: On min bound, we set 10 because we didn’t want to pay overnight. But we’ve noticed the first 2-3 minutes after ramp starts can be bumpy.

[09:13] Vanessa Ortiz: That’s consistent: if you start too low, even with predictive, you may be catching up. Predictive helps but it’s not magic if you’re under-provisioned at T0.

[09:24] Jenna Wu: Could we do min 12 during business hours and 10 off-hours?

[09:29] Vanessa Ortiz: Not in product yet as a schedule, but we can do it manually or via your IaC if you have a script. In pilot, we can do a manual change at 8am central, but that’s not ideal.

[09:41] Liam O'Rourke: Some customers are doing it with Terraform, but I think the provider support is still in progress. For pilot, we can do manual changes and record them.

[09:51] Omar Rahman: Manual is okay for a week. Not long term.

[09:55] Rachel Kim: Understood. We’ll capture “scheduled bounds” as a product request.

[10:00] Mark Feldman: Another question: When prediction is wrong, does reactive override it immediately? Because sometimes it feels like prediction is saying “down” while reactive is saying “up.”

[10:10] Vanessa Ortiz: The way it works in the pilot: we compute a predicted desired, we compute a reactive desired, then we take the higher of the two for scale-up safety, but for scale-down we apply dampening and we also won’t scale down if reactive signals are still indicating saturation or queueing. Then we clamp.

[10:30] Mark Feldman: Okay. So scale-up is basically max(pred, reactive) then clamp to max.

[10:35] Vanessa Ortiz: Exactly.

[10:37] Priya Desai: And scale-down is like… more conservative.

[10:40] Vanessa Ortiz: Yes, and we can make it more conservative still by increasing cooldown.

[10:46] Sergio Costa: On this dashboard, the “prediction vs actual” panel is here, but it’s a little rough. It’s basically forecasted req/sec vs actual. There’s also a staleness indicator, but it’s not super visible.

[10:58] Jenna Wu: That’s another thing. The UI didn’t tell us the prediction was stale. If it was stale, that explains some weirdness.

[11:05] Vanessa Ortiz: That’s good feedback. We do have a staleness check, and if it’s too stale we should fall back to reactive only. If we didn’t, that’s a bug.

[11:16] Mark Feldman: That might be what happened on Friday when desired went to zero.

[11:20] Vanessa Ortiz: Potentially. Let me confirm.

[11:23] Rachel Kim: Okay, we’ll treat that as a bug to investigate.

[11:27] Rachel Kim: Switching gears: overall, how are you feeling about the “hard bounds” behavior? Is it meeting the original goal?

[11:34] Omar Rahman: Yes. Like, I can sleep at night knowing we won’t blow past a ceiling. Before, we got surprised. This is better.

[11:42] Priya Desai: Same. But operationally, we need the “you’re capped” notification to be more explicit.

[11:48] Jenna Wu: And we need guidance on picking the numbers. Like, do we set max to meet peak plus 10%? Or do we accept queue? It’s more a product decision.

[11:58] Rachel Kim: That’s fair. We can provide a recommended range based on your last 14 days. Not contractual, but guidance.

[12:05] Vanessa Ortiz: We can also run a quick simulation — if max were 28 vs 24, what would p95 have been. We have a replay harness internally.

[12:14] Mark Feldman: That would be awesome.

[12:16] Liam O'Rourke: If we can do that, we can justify the budget increase.

[12:20] Omar Rahman: Exactly.

[12:22] Sergio Costa: For today, should we decide on 28? Then we evaluate Thursday.

[12:28] Priya Desai: Yes. I can apply that change. What’s the process, do I do it in Console or do you do it?

[12:35] Rachel Kim: For pilot, we can do either. If your Console has the bounds form enabled, you can edit max. If not, Liam can request it through the internal admin.

[12:44] Liam O'Rourke: I think Hexagon is enabled for the UI. Priya, you should see “Scaling policy” in the deployment settings.

[12:50] Priya Desai: I see it, yes.

[12:52] Liam O'Rourke: Great. Just note it should log who changed it and when.

[12:56] Priya Desai: Perfect. I’ll do it after this call.

[13:00] Mark Feldman: Any risk to changing max on the fly?

[13:03] Vanessa Ortiz: No functional risk. It just changes the clamp. The autoscaler loop will respect it next evaluation cycle.

[13:09] Jenna Wu: Can it cause immediate scale up and create thundering herd?

[13:14] Vanessa Ortiz: We rate-limit step size. So it won’t go from 24 to 28 instantly unless your step size allows it. It will ramp.

[13:22] Mark Feldman: Good.

[13:23] Rachel Kim: Okay. On min: do we want to change min from 10 to 12 for this week, or keep it and just adjust max?

[13:31] Omar Rahman: If we bump min, we pay more overnight, right?

[13:35] Priya Desai: Overnight we’re pretty low traffic. But the ramp at 9am is the pain.

[13:41] Vanessa Ortiz: One approach: keep min 10, but adjust predictive lead time so it ramps earlier. But if we have a staleness issue, that’s not stable. Another approach: set min 12 temporarily and see if the ramp smooths.

[13:54] Jenna Wu: I’d prefer min 12 during weekdays, but I don’t want to babysit it every day.

[14:01] Liam O'Rourke: For pilot, we can just set min 12 now and accept the extra baseline for one week. It’s the simplest. Then later we add scheduling.

[14:10] Omar Rahman: What’s the delta cost? Two GPUs * 24/7 is not nothing.

[14:15] Rachel Kim: We can estimate, but since this is pilot, we can treat it as part of the evaluation. For production you’d decide based on SLA.

[14:23] Omar Rahman: Okay, but I want it in writing: “pilot configuration change, expected cost increase.”

[14:28] Rachel Kim: Yep, I’ll send a recap email with estimated impact.

[14:33] Mark Feldman: Also, if the max alert works, we can maybe keep min lower and just know when we’re saturating.

[14:39] Vanessa Ortiz: True, but alerts don’t fix user experience.

[14:43] Jenna Wu: Yeah. Users don’t care that we got an email.

[14:46] Rachel Kim: Right. Okay, how about: max to 28 now, keep min at 10 for two days, then if Thursday ramp still spikes, we consider min 12. That way we isolate variables.

[14:58] Priya Desai: That sounds reasonable.

[15:01] Omar Rahman: Agreed.

[15:03] Sergio Costa: Works.

[15:05] Rachel Kim: Great. Now, the bug: “desired=0” in Console. Priya, can you send us screenshot plus approximate time, and we’ll correlate with logs?

[15:13] Priya Desai: Yes.

[15:15] Liam O'Rourke: If you can include the deployment id or URL, even better.

[15:19] Priya Desai: Will do.

[15:21] Mark Feldman: We also saw one case where predictive seemed to scale down while queue depth was still non-zero. Is that possible?

[15:28] Vanessa Ortiz: It shouldn’t. If queue depth is above threshold, reactive desired should be higher and scale-down should be blocked. Unless queue depth metric was delayed or missing.

[15:39] Sergio Costa: Metric delay is possible. We ingest with ~10-20s latency usually, but if there was a scrape issue it could be worse.

[15:47] Mark Feldman: Okay. It was brief.

[15:49] Vanessa Ortiz: Let’s treat it as “investigate with timestamps.” If it’s real, we’ll adjust the guard: don’t scale down if queue depth > 0 for N seconds.

[16:01] Jenna Wu: Another request: can we get a “confidence” indicator for predictive? Like if it’s low confidence, don’t use it.

[16:09] Vanessa Ortiz: We have an internal notion of forecast quality and staleness. We’re not surfacing confidence yet. It’s on the roadmap, but we can at least surface “forecast stale / forecast missing.”

[16:21] Rachel Kim: That’s probably the MVP we can do soon.

[16:25] Omar Rahman: For FinOps, the main thing is: don’t scale up due to prediction if it’s garbage.

[16:31] Vanessa Ortiz: Understood. That’s why reactive override exists. For scale-up, we’re taking the max, so prediction can only increase, but it can’t exceed max. So worst case it uses budget early but still within cap.

[16:45] Omar Rahman: Okay.

[16:46] Rachel Kim: Switching to alerts: Sergio, can you propose an alert for sustained max bound + queue depth? Mark said email, not page.

[16:55] Sergio Costa: Yes. I’ll draft something like: “bounded==max for 5m AND queue_depth_p95 > X” or something. We need to pick X.

[17:06] Mark Feldman: We can start with a low threshold, like queue depth over 50 for more than 3 minutes.

[17:12] Jenna Wu: 50 might be too low. Our normal blips can hit 30.

[17:16] Mark Feldman: Okay, 100.

[17:18] Rachel Kim: Let’s keep it flexible. Sergio will propose a threshold based on your baseline.

[17:23] Sergio Costa: Yep, I’ll look at your last week and pick something that’s not noisy.

[17:28] Liam O'Rourke: And we can route it to a distro list, maybe “hexagon-llm-oncall@”?

[17:34] Mark Feldman: Yes.

[17:36] Rachel Kim: Great. Anything else? Jenna, any product feedback from the app teams?

[17:42] Jenna Wu: They like that the ramps are better than before, but they still feel like the first ten minutes of the day are a little rough. That’s why we’re pushing on predictive.

[17:53] Rachel Kim: Makes sense.

[17:55] Priya Desai: One more thing: timezone. Our ramp is in central time, but I’m not sure your predictor is using our timezone or UTC. Could that cause the pre-scale to happen at the wrong time?

[18:07] Vanessa Ortiz: Forecasts are keyed to UTC right now, but we align based on your historical traffic. If your traffic pattern is consistent, it shouldn’t matter, but if daylight savings or your schedule changes, it can misalign. That’s something we’re working on.

[18:22] Priya Desai: Okay. Because Monday it scaled up at like 7:45am, which is early.

[18:28] Omar Rahman: That’s money.

[18:30] Vanessa Ortiz: Yeah. That could be the predictor overshooting. Another reason to add “confidence” and/or reduce lead time.

[18:39] Rachel Kim: Great. We’ll capture this as feedback.

…

[30:12] Sergio Costa: Quick note: the dashboard link I sent is scoped by deployment_id, so if you change bounds, it will still show before/after. I’ll annotate the panels, because right now the labels are a bit jargon-y.

[30:25] Priya Desai: Yes please. The “unbounded” wording confused one of our engineers.

[30:31] Sergio Costa: Got it.

…

[39:44] Rachel Kim: Alright, let’s recap decisions so we’re aligned.

[39:48] Rachel Kim: 1) Priya will update max bound from 24 to 28 today after the call, for the pilot week.

[39:55] Priya Desai: Yes.

[39:56] Rachel Kim: 2) We keep min at 10 for now to isolate the change. If Thursday ramp still shows queue/p95 spikes, we revisit min 12.

[40:06] Omar Rahman: Yep.

[40:07] Rachel Kim: 3) Redwood investigates the “desired=0 / predictor null” UI/audit confusion. Priya will send screenshot + timestamp. Vanessa will pull logs and confirm whether it’s display-only or a real decision path.

[40:21] Vanessa Ortiz: Yep.

[40:22] Priya Desai: Yep.

[40:23] Rachel Kim: 4) Sergio drafts an email alert proposal for sustained max-bound saturation, routed to email distro, not paging.

[40:32] Sergio Costa: Yes.

[40:34] Rachel Kim: 5) Rachel (me) will send a recap email including expected cost impact of max 28 and guidance on interpreting desired vs bounded.

[40:44] Jenna Wu: Great.

[40:46] Mark Feldman: Can we schedule next meeting for Friday same time? After the Thursday ramp.

[40:52] Liam O'Rourke: Works for us.

[40:53] Rachel Kim: Great, we’ll send the invite.

[40:56] Rachel Kim: Anything else before we drop?

[40:59] Mark Feldman: That’s it.

[41:00] Priya Desai: Thanks.

[41:01] Omar Rahman: Thanks.

[41:02] Rachel Kim: Thanks everyone.

---

Auto-generated notes (may be inaccurate)
- Key moment: deployment capped at max bound (24) during morning ramp; desired_unbounded ~31; queue depth increased.
- Customer request: clearer “capped by policy” indicator + alerting.
- Bug: Console/audit view showed desired=0 briefly; bounded capacity did not drop below min.
- Next: raise max to 28; investigate predictor null/staleness + timezone alignment; tune scale-down cooldown.
